task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer about book and online-access costs in a Fenwick College course, answering why a cheaper used textbook may not be the cheapest way to obtain all required materials.

facts.text: Fenwick College's autumn 2026 introductory accounting course uses the original fictional textbook Ledgers in Practice and an associated online problem platform.
The campus bookstore lists a new book-and-platform bundle at $96.
Its used print copy costs $28 and does not include an unused platform code.
The publisher sells a standalone semester platform code for $70, making that code plus the used book $98.
The platform code also includes a digital version of the textbook, so a print copy is not required to read the assigned text.
The code is assigned to one student and expires at the end of the semester under the supplied terms.
Buying a used book does not transfer another student's already activated code.
The college library has six print reserve copies available for short loans but those loans do not provide platform accounts.
Instructor Omi Brack says the platform is used for scheduled homework submission, not merely optional extra reading.
The instructor offers a no-charge offline assignment route to students who arrange it through the course office.
The offline route uses the same assessed topics but requires a different submission process and does not include a personal digital book license.
Student Rella Vale wants a print copy because she annotates pages during her commute.
Vale said, "The used book is cheaper until I add the thing the assignment asks me to log into."
Publisher representative Neri Doss says the separate platform price pays for hosted exercises and updates rather than only a digital copy of printed pages.
Doss said, "The book and the account travel together in a bundle, but they are not the same product."
The reporting record does not provide the publisher's platform costs or profit margin.
There are 150 enrolled students, but the college has not counted how many will choose bundles, standalone access or the offline route.
The bookstore's prices are dated August 2026 and do not establish every secondhand seller's price.
The bookstore operates an annual used-book exchange for courses that do not use single-user access codes.
The supplied policies describe this course and do not establish that every college course requires a paid platform.

forbidden_additions: The used book includes a transferable account or every student must buy both print and digital products
No offline alternative, a verified publisher margin or universal college policy
